organization.name: Nethermind
organization.summary: Company building Ethereum infrastructure. Its website lists core protocol development, execution node engineering, EVM research, applied cryptography, ZK systems and formal methods. The Nethermind execution client repository on GitHub was created 2017-08-23.

previousFunding.label: Ethereum Foundation 2024 Academic Grants (EVM and Yul in Lean)

delivery.grant: Ethereum Foundation 2024 Academic Grants: Towards an Executable Formal Model of EVM and Yul in Lean
delivery.promised: Per the EF recipients page: a project that formalizes the EVM in Lean, providing tools for reasoning about smart contracts and execution environments. The proposal says previous EF funding supported Cancun formalisation. The EF page does not mention Cancun, so the link between the two statements is not confirmed.

claims.claim: LeanCIL is a public repository for formal verification of compiled .NET code in Lean 4.
claims.method: GitHub API: public repository created 2026-10-14, last push 2026-11-28, 131 stars, license reported as NOASSERTION. The README describes extracting CIL from .NET assemblies and checking proofs in Lean 4, with example proofs. Proofs were not rerun. The proposal itself says LeanCIL does not yet cover the full EVM.

claims.claim: bflat-riscv64 is a compiler supporting ZisK, SP1 and OpenVM.
claims.method: GitHub API: public AGPL-3.0 repository created 2025-04-16, last push 2026-11-24. The README target table lists zisk, sp1 and openvm targets. Compilation was not run.

claims.claim: EVMYulLean is an executable formal model of the EVM and Yul in Lean 4.
claims.method: GitHub API: public Apache-2.0 repository created 2024-07-18, last push 2025-11-19, 102 stars. The README describes the model and states everything is work in progress.

claims.claim: EthLib defines and proves EVM rules in Lean, with some Amsterdam gaps.
claims.method: The repository exists (public, CC0-1.0, last push 2026-11-28, 112 stars). The Amsterdam coverage was not reviewed.

claims.claim: Ben Adams is co-author of 15 Core EIPs and a twelve-time Microsoft MVP.
claims.method: Not checked against the EIP repository or a Microsoft MVP profile. The GitHub profile exists (login benaadams, created 2011-10-21).
